## Professional Background

Vasilis Totskas develops applications for web, desktop and mobile, and builds the infrastructure that runs them. He has worked professionally since July 2020, when he joined Advisable as an intern; he has been a web developer there since January 2021.

Since August 2026 he is also serving his military service as a full stack engineer at ΚΕ.Π.Υ.Ε.Σ. in the Greek Army, building applications with FastAPI and Angular on Oracle Database.

At Advisable he works on complex web applications, modernising technology stacks and delivering projects on standalone PHP, TypeScript and Python stacks as well as Nuxt 4 frontends.

Outside that role he builds and operates GrooveShop, a multi-tenant e-commerce platform, and runs it in production for a real store. Building the product and operating the infrastructure it runs on are the same job for him — the self-hosted Kubernetes cluster behind webside.gr is his own.

## Notable Projects

### GrooveShop — e-commerce platform
A multi-tenant, multi-repository e-commerce platform built over more than four years. Each store is its own PostgreSQL schema, resolved from the request host, with its own domain, theme, credentials and feature switches (loyalty, gift cards, promotions, B2B). Four stores run on it, including the demo. It is made of five components:

- **Django REST API** — business logic, authentication and data
- **Nuxt 4 storefront** — SSR frontend; its Nitro server proxies `/api/...` calls to Django after validating them with Zod
- **NestJS media stream** — standalone image processing and media delivery; the frontend builds URLs pointing straight at it
- **Go agent gateway** — makes every tenant storefront shoppable by AI agents: an MCP server over stateless HTTP with commerce tools (search, products, categories, shipping, cart, checkout, order tracking), UCP/ACP surfaces for agentic checkout, product feeds for Google Merchant, Meta, TikTok and ACP, and an SSE backend powering a storefront chatbot
- **Infrastructure** — PostgreSQL, Redis, Meilisearch, RabbitMQ and Celery workers, on K3s and synced by Argo CD

Built-in commerce: a rule-based promotion engine, stored-value gift cards, loyalty points with tiers, a wholesale programme with VIES VAT validation, Viva Wallet and Stripe payments, ACS and BoxNow shipping, and Meilisearch search with Greeklish transliteration.

Case study: https://www.vasilistotskas.com/en/projects/grooveshop
Live demo: https://demo.grooveshop.space/
Documentation: https://docs.grooveshop.space
Repositories: https://github.com/vasilistotskas/grooveshop-django-api, https://github.com/vasilistotskas/grooveshop-storefront-ui-node-nuxt, https://github.com/vasilistotskas/grooveshop-media-stream, https://github.com/vasilistotskas/grooveshop-agent-gateway (the infrastructure repository is private)

### Webside.gr
A production e-commerce store for phone and computer accessories, one tenant of GrooveShop since August 2026. It has taken real orders since May 2026: more than 200 orders and more than €6,000 in revenue (cancelled and returned orders excluded). It runs every layer of the platform on self-hosted infrastructure:

- Hetzner k3s Kubernetes cluster
- ArgoCD for GitOps deployment
- Longhorn for distributed storage
- RabbitMQ for message queuing
- Celery for background task processing
- Redis for caching
- Cert-Manager for automated TLS certificates

Releases go through Argo CD sync hooks: a pre-sync job checks migrations are safe, migrates every tenant schema, collects static files and applies the Meilisearch index settings; post-sync jobs purge the Cloudflare edge cache and warm the storefront.

Case study: https://www.vasilistotskas.com/en/projects/webside
Live: https://webside.gr

### Developer portfolio (this site)
- Next.js 16 (App Router, Turbopack), React 19, TypeScript strict
- Tailwind CSS v4, CSS-first configuration with no `tailwind.config`
- next-intl v4 for English and Greek; `app/[locale]/layout.tsx` is the root layout so `next/root-params` resolves
- IBM Plex Sans and JetBrains Mono, both loaded with the Greek subset
- A WebGPU hero rendered with vgpu: one fullscreen WGSL fragment shader drawing the shape of source code — indentation, runs of identifiers, blank lines between blocks, a caret and a parse wave. It pauses off screen and when the tab is hidden, renders a single still frame under `prefers-reduced-motion`, and renders nothing at all without WebGPU, leaving a CSS gradient in its place
- A command palette opened with `/`, or from a header button on touch
- Spotify integration (now playing, top tracks) and GitHub statistics
- Deployed to Vercel through GitHub Actions; releases automated with semantic-release

Live: https://www.vasilistotskas.com
Source: https://github.com/vasilistotskas/nextjs-portfolio

## Technical Implementation Details

### Theming
- Semantic CSS variables for light and dark, switched by a `light`/`dark` class on `<html>`
- Dark by default; the choice is stored in `localStorage` under `theme`
- A pre-paint script is injected into `<head>` through `useServerInsertedHTML`, so there is no flash of the wrong theme
- Colour tokens: terminal-bg, terminal-surface, terminal-text, terminal-green, terminal-muted, terminal-comment, terminal-prompt, terminal-yellow. One accent colour, green
- Custom utilities: `.glass`, `.glass-blur`, `.glow-green`, `.card-hover`, `.terminal-border`, `.stack-fallback`

### Fonts
- IBM Plex Sans (interface)
- JetBrains Mono (code, labels and the command palette)
- Both loaded with `subsets: ['latin', 'greek']`, because the Greek pages need Greek glyphs

### API Routes
All run on the default Node runtime.

- `/api/contact` — email delivery through Resend
- `/api/spotify/now-playing` — current or most recent track
- `/api/spotify/top-tracks` — top tracks over a selectable range

GitHub statistics are fetched directly by a Server Component; there is no `/api/github` route.
